name: Read the Docs
description: Read the Docs is a documentation building and hosting platform that treats documentation like code: it connects to Git repositories, builds docs automatically on every commit, and gives every pull request a live preview.
best_for: Open source and community projects (free tier) as well as commercial and enterprise engineering teams (paid plans starting around $50/month) that want documentation infrastructure handled for them.
features: Git integration with automatic doc builds on every commit
Pull request previews with visual diffs against production
Support for multiple documentation tools, including Sphinx, MkDocs, and Docusaurus
Versioned documentation built automatically from branches or tags
SSO access control via GitHub or GitLab on paid plans
Private repository support via connected Git accounts or SSH keys
llms.txt and Markdown content negotiation for AI tool compatibility

alternatives.name: Docusaurus
alternatives.description: An open source static site generator for building documentation websites with Markdown/MDX and React.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want full control of their doc site's design and want to self-host the output.

alternatives.name: GitBook
alternatives.description: A knowledge management platform for creating and publishing product and technical documentation.
alternatives.best_for: Teams that want a visual editor with Git sync rather than a static-site build pipeline.

pricing.starting_price: Free for eligible open-source projects; Business plans start at $50/month

tiers.name: Community
tiers.notes: Free for open-source projects using public repositories and public, ad-supported documentation hosting.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.notes: Two concurrent builds, a shared domain, GitHub/GitLab SSO, 50 redirects, and three-business-day support.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.notes: Four concurrent builds, five custom domains, 250 redirects, and two-business-day support.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.notes: Six concurrent builds, 15 custom domains, Google SSO, 500 redirects, and one-business-day support.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Starts at $10,000/year and adds SAML SSO, dedicated builders, advanced audit tracking, and a support SLA.

pros: Community hosting remains free for eligible open-source documentation projects
Paid plans include a 30-day trial and publish numeric monthly prices rather than requiring a sales call at entry tiers
Every paid plan includes automatic builds, versioning, search, pull-request previews, and CDN hosting
cons: The free Community option is for public open-source projects and uses ad-supported hosting; commercial or private documentation requires Business plans
Custom domains are not included on the $50 Basic plan and start on Advanced
Enterprise starts at $10,000 per year, creating a large step above the $250/month Pro plan

faq.question: Is Read the Docs free?
faq.answer: Read the Docs Community is free for open-source projects with public repositories and public documentation. Commercial and private documentation use the paid Business product.

faq.question: How much does Read the Docs Business cost?
faq.answer: The published monthly prices are $50 for Basic, $150 for Advanced, and $250 for Pro. Enterprise starts at $10,000 per year.

faq.question: Does Read the Docs offer a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. The Business pricing page offers a 30-day trial and says the account is not charged automatically when the trial ends.
